tip: Repeated trips by vehicle use ездил (yezdil = went), the there-and-back form: часто ездил (chasta yezdil) means going there regularly and back.
водил (vadil = took) is the there-and-back form for leading someone somewhere over and over, unlike one-trip ведёт (vedyot).
везёт (vezyot = is taking) is the one-direction form for transporting by vehicle right now toward a single place.
ведёт (vedyot = is leading) is the one-direction form for taking someone on foot to one place now, unlike repeated водит (vodit).
Means of transport uses на (na = on) plus the prepositional: на поезде (na poezde = by train).
The more, the more pairs чем (chem) with тем (tem): чем больше читаешь, тем умнее (chem bolshe chitaesh, tem umneye = the more you read, the smarter).
In compound years only the last word takes the ordinal ending: девяносто первый (devyanosta pervyy = ninety first); earlier parts stay plain numbers.
Traveling by car uses на (na = on) plus the prepositional: на машине (na mashine = by car).
достичь (dastich = to reach) takes the genitive, not the accusative: достиг вершины (dastig vershiny = reached the summit).
так и не (tak i ne = never did) plus a completed-action verb marks a planned thing that never got done: так и не доделали (tak i ne dadelali = never finished it).
Imperfective учил (uchil = studied) names the effort; perfective выучил (vyuchil = learned) names the result, here denied by так и не (tak i ne).
The tool used takes the instrumental with no preposition: молотком и зубилом (malatkom i zubilam = with hammer and chisel).
куда (kuda = where to) asks about direction with motion verbs, unlike где (gde = where) for a fixed location.
The -ся on открывается (atkryvaetsya = opens) means it acts on its own: the door opens by itself, no object needed.
вёз (vyoz) is past of везти (vezti = carry by vehicle), used when the load moves by transport, not carried by hand.
The -ся on целуются (tseluyutsya = kiss) makes it mutual: they kiss each other, not themselves.
A place entered with на (na) is exited with с (s), not из (iz): с вечеринки (s vecherinki = from the party).
над (nad = over) takes the instrumental case: над озером (nad ozeram = over the lake).
шли (shli = were going) comes from идти (idti), the one-direction verb for a single trip toward рынок (rynak = market).
часто (chasta = often) triggers the round-trip verb: бегал (begal = ran there and back), not one-way бежал (bezhal).
носить (nasit) means carry, but with очки (achki = glasses) or clothes it means wear: носит очки (nosit achki = wears glasses).
помогать (pamagat) takes the dative, so the person helped is мне (mne = me), not accusative: помогал мне (pamagal mne = helped me).
Being late uses опоздать (apazdat) with на (na) plus accusative: опоздал на работу (apazdal na rabotu = late for work).
звонить (zvanit) takes the dative, so the person you call stands in dative and the question word is кому (kamu = to whom), as in звонил (zvanil).
не хватает (ne khvataet = lacks) is impersonal: the person is dative ему (emu = to him) and the missing thing is genitive времени (vremeni = time).
в гости (v gosti = for a visit) is a fixed phrase for going to visit someone, used here with привёл (privyol = brought).
After a large number the noun goes genitive plural: шестьсот граммов (shestsot grammav = six hundred grams).
из-за (iz-za = because of) marks a negative cause and takes the genitive: из-за новостей (iz-za navastey = because of the news).
For transport, на (na) plus the prepositional case means by that vehicle: на метро (na metro = by metro).
помоги (pamagi = help) is the informal command of помочь (pamoch), the ты (ty) form used with friends, family, or children.
